item.title: Worldwide Heat — 2026-05-10
item.content:encoded:
# Worldwide Heat — 2026-05-10
**The Chemical Brothers — Go** (2015)
Netflix's thriller *Apex* is the reason a decade-old Chemical Brothers track is currently sitting at number one on Shazam and dominating streaming charts globally. The film's director Baltasar Kormákur told [Decider via Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chemical-brothers-go-apex-movie-streaming-boost-netflix-1236241050/) that star Taron Egerton personally sourced the track for a key scene — one in which a character puts on a song and promises to give chase once it ends — and the placement turned out to be a near-perfect union of tension and sound. U.S. on-demand streams jumped from 92,000 to 487,000 in a single week, with daily plays peaking at 127,000 on April 30, according to [Music Times](https://www.musictimes.com/articles/111818/20260507/netflixs-apex-sends-chemical-brothers-go-massive-streaming-comeback.htm). The clip from that scene has accumulated tens of millions of views across TikTok and Instagram, per [We Rave You](https://weraveyou.com/2026/05/chemical-brothers-go-netflix-apex-viral/). Originally released as the second single from *Born in the Echoes* — featuring uncredited vocals from Q-Tip — "Go" earned a Grammy nomination in 2015 before settling into cult status. The 429% streaming surge, reported by [Ace Showbiz](https://www.aceshowbiz.com/news/view/00257251.html), has also pushed it to number five on the Dance Digital Song Sales chart, a commercial lane the track never cracked the first time around.

---
**Justin Bieber, Nicki Minaj — Beauty And A Beat** (2012)
Bieber's buzzy Coachella performances have sent a 13-year-old club track to the top of the global charts. According to [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/justin-bieber-beauty-and-a-beat-global-charts-may-9-1236238395/), "Beauty and a Beat" is currently No. 1 on both the Billboard Global 200 and the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart, while [a Threads post tracking Spotify data](https://www.threads.com/@hiphopfreakz/post/DXKYJkxD3NS/justin-bieber-and-nicki-minajs-song-beauty-and-a-beat-which-was-released-back) reported 7.43 million streams in a single day after the Coachella performance aired. The event generated an additional subplot: per [AOL](https://www.aol.com/articles/justin-bieber-skips-nicki-minaj-100300133.html), Bieber cut the track before Nicki Minaj's verse, which produced over 200,000 TikTok posts in three days and a public response from Minaj herself — a side story that kept the song in feeds well after the set ended. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2026/04/30/justin-biebers-decade-old-dance-smash-climbs-to-no-1-globally/) notes the song only entered these rankings the week prior, making the jump to No. 1 unusually rapid for catalog material. The last non-holiday catalog track to reach No. 1 on the Global Excl. U.S. was Kate Bush's "Running Up That Hill" in 2022, driven by its *Stranger Things* sync — a very different kind of cultural ignition than a live performance.
---
**Michael Jackson — Billie Jean** (1982)
The *Michael* biopic has triggered the largest streaming week of Michael Jackson's catalog in recorded history, and Billie Jean is leading the charge. According to [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/michael-jackson-best-streaming-week-after-michael-movie-1236240552/), the track is sitting at No. 5 on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, and per [That Grape Juice](https://thatgrapejuice.net/2026/05/chart-check-michael-jacksons-thriller-billie-jean-bounce-back-to-billboard-glory-amid-biopic-success/), it has climbed to No. 38 on the Hot 100. In the UK, [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2026/04/28/michael-jacksons-classic-smash-dances-to-a-new-chart-peak/) reports it has surged to a new peak on the Official Streaming chart while also re-entering the Official Singles tally. The song is now appearing broadly across charts in well over a hundred countries. The biopic effect on catalog is a well-documented phenomenon — *Bohemian Rhapsody* and *Rocketman* both produced multi-week streaming surges for their subjects — but the scale here, with ten Jackson titles simultaneously on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, places this in a different tier.

**Foo Fighters — Iron Rooster** (2015)
> *Have you ever been dumb enough to do what you wanted to do* > *Without good reason coming over you?* > *Have you ever been young enough to feel what you wanted to feel?* > *Take back those years for something real*
"Iron Rooster" is broadly charting today on the strength of a live revival that has made one of the rarest tracks in the Foo Fighters catalog suddenly visible again. According to [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/lists/foo-fighters-irving-plaza-best-moments/), the band performed the song at a recent underplay in New York — only the fourth time this year, and just the eighth time ever, following a 25-year performance hiatus. That kind of concentrated scarcity tends to push catalog curiosity hard: listeners who caught word of the show go looking for the recording.
The track originally appeared on the *Saint Cecilia* EP, released free in November 2015 as a goodwill gesture to fans. No specific film or TV placement for this song has surfaced in available reporting. What's driving the current chart presence appears to be the live-show story alone — a rare enough event that it functions as its own news cycle. For a deep cut that spent a decade largely unplayed, eight performances in a single year amounts to a second life.
---
**Bethel Music, Amanda Cook — I Belong to You (Live)**
A live worship recording released in 2014 is appearing on streaming charts for the first time, across 144 country and platform cells simultaneously. The track appears on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/track/6DQ7OllUB6LskI1fmRlJGT) credited to Bethel Music and vocalist Amanda Cook, who has been a central figure in the Redding, California-based worship collective's catalog. Bethel Music occupies an unusual position in the streaming landscape — producing music built for congregational use that periodically crosses into general listening charts without conventional promotion. The dossier does not identify a specific driver for the current spike. Twelve years between release and first chart appearance is an outlier even by catalog-revival standards; the breadth of today's debut — 144 cells simultaneously — suggests the movement is not confined to a single region or platform.
